newsitem.title: MEXICO: Penoles issues $380 mln in notes.
newsitem.headline: Penoles issues $380 mln in notes.

text.p: Mexico's Industrias Penoles SA, the world's largest producer of refined silver, said on Wednesday it had issued $380 million in "structured silver payable notes," debt optionally payable in silver.
The company said the innovative, 15-year notes had a rate of 190 basis points above U.S. Treasuries and was placed among private investors in the United States, principally insurance companies.
"These notes have a structure which gives holders the option to receive debt servicing payment in kind -- that is, in equivalent silver ounces," the company said in a statement.
Merrill Lynch was lead agent on the deal.

Penoles said the notes had received an investment grade rating of BBB from Standard and Poors, the first time a Mexican company has bettered the country's sovereign debt rating without export guarantees or an international financial institution.
The company said it was originally going to issue just $280 million in notes, but because of heavy demand decided to boost the issue.
Penoles said it would use the money in part to fund two gold mines, known as Mezcala and Herradura, and one zinc mine, Francisco Madero.
It said it will also use the money to expand its Met-Mex zinc plant, expand other unspecified mines, and bid for Peru's state-owned Mataloroya mine.
